Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer
Email: [EMAIL] | Phone: [PHONE]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing and operating Azure environments, building infrastructure as code with Terraform, and automating deployments with Azure DevOps. Background includes Azure landing-zone networking, AKS operations, infrastructure security, and migration of virtualized workloads to Azure. Previously administered around 250 Windows and Linux servers in a municipal IT department.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and platforms: Microsoft Azure, Azure VMs, Azure Migrate, AKS, App Service, Microsoft 365, Entra ID
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, PowerShell, Python (small scripts), Go (Terratest tests)
CI/CD and containers: Azure DevOps Pipelines, YAML pipelines, Docker, Helm
Networking: Hub-and-spoke networks, VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN
Security: MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, backups
Systems: Windows, Linux, VMware, Proxmox

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build Azure landing-zone infrastructure and Terraform modules.
- Designed hub-and-spoke networking across three Azure subscriptions, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments of 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS, including upgrades, node pools, and ingress.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines.
- Enabled MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups for small clients.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–March 2020
- Administered around 250 Windows and Linux servers and supported staff across several municipal services.
- Planned and executed the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Used PowerShell to automate repetitive work.

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Career break | March 2020–August 2022
- Took a career break to provide full-time care for a family member; provided unpaid IT help to church and family.

Career break and professional development | February 2024–February 2025
- Completed a three-month, part-time, online English-language cloud bootcamp in December 2024.
- Studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (2025)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role supporting Corvale Mobility’s fleet connectivity platform. In my current contract as a Cloud Engineer, I build Azure infrastructure with Terraform, operate AKS, and create deployment pipelines that help move services into production reliably.

At Havenstad Logistics, I designed a hub-and-spoke Azure network spanning three subscriptions, with Azure Firewall, private DNS, private endpoints, and peering. I also added Terratest module tests and nightly drift detection. For internal applications, I replaced manual releases with Azure DevOps pipelines for 15 .NET and Node apps, raising deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most apps. This work has given me practical experience with infrastructure design, networking, automation, and supporting application delivery.

Earlier, I planned and carried out a migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS, completing the cut-over over six weekends without unplanned downtime. My systems administration background also includes Windows and Linux environments, while my freelance work included PowerShell-based Microsoft 365 security baselines. Corvale’s project to connect a new generation of trains with cloud services is a compelling opportunity to apply this infrastructure experience to a platform being shaped from the start and taken into production.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my Azure, Terraform, networking, and delivery-pipeline experience could contribute to Corvale’s fleet connectivity work. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
